newsitem.title: USA: Owens sees steady growth in Richmond Fed District.
newsitem.headline: Owens sees steady growth in Richmond Fed District.

text.p: Steady growth still appears to be the most plausible scenario for the Fifth Federal Reserve District in the coming year, an economist with the Richmond Fed said Tuesday.
"It appears that the steady, modest growth apparently is pretty well grounded going into 1997," Richmond Fed economist Raymond Owens told Reuters Financial Television.
The Richmond Fed District includes the District of Columbia, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia and most of West Virginia.
Earlier, the Richmond Fed reported that its indexes of manufacturing and service activity were mixed in December.
The manufacturing shipments index fell to -2 in the month from 0 in November, while new orders fell to 2 from 5 in November.
The service revenues index was unchanged in December at 5.

Asked what some of the risks in the report were, Owens replied, "The major concerns are that prices could pick up a little too much. Certainly we're seeing some evidence of increasing wage pressures."

Another risk he cited was "perhaps (that) the manufacturing sector would continue to struggle and those sectors that are exhibiting weakness now wouldn't turn around as quickly as we would perhaps hope."
